This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER Heard.
Perused the case diary.
2. This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail.

The applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.355/2022,
registered at Police Station Jawad, District Neemuch, for the offences punishable under Sections 34(2), 49 of M.P. Excise Act and Section 420 and 482 of the IPC.

3. As per the prosecution, on 29.8.2022, on receipt of a secret information co-accused Ganpat and Manoharlal Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141208194/
1

entities.text: Ganpat and Manoharlal Sen vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Ganesh were arrested while they were transporting total 60 litres and 480 ML of illicit country made liquor without a valid license.

Thereafter their memorandum under Section 27 of the Evidence Act were recorded in which they stated to have procured the liquor from co- accused Manish Kumawat who in his memorandum stated to have procured the same from co-accused Anil and Manish.

Thereafter memorandum of Anil was recorded in which he stated that the equipments of manufacture of liquor had been supplied to him by the applicant on the basis of which he has been implicated for the present offence.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
There is no evidence direct or indirect to connect him with the present crime.
Besides the memorandum of co- accused recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act there is no other material on record to implicate him with the present crime.
The memorandum is even otherwise a third memorandum and the allegation against the applicant is only of supplying the material for manufacturing the liquor and not the liquor for itself.
On such grounds, prayer for grant of benefit of anticipatory bail to the applicant has been made.

5. The aforesaid prayer has been opposed by the learned counsel for the respondent/State submitting that in view of the allegations levelled against the applicant he is not entitled for grant of benefit of anticipatory bail.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have perused the case diary.
7. The implication of the applicant appears to be primarily on the basis of third memorandum of co-accused recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act.
There is no material to directly or indirectly implicate the applicant with the present crime.
The applicant is not shown to be having any criminal antecedents.
Thus in my opinion, the applicant deserves to be granted the benefit of anticipatory bail.

8. It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicant by the Arresting Officer, he shall be released on bail subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- with two solvent sureties of Rs.25,000/- each out of which one shall be local surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
9. The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.

Applicant shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.
10.
This order shall be subject to the condition that the applicant shall appear before the trial court on the next date of hearing and shall furnish his bail bonds.
11. Accordingly, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.31641/2023, stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
